findings.statement: Request a Gong developer instance through the partner application form on collective.gong.io; setup can take up to five working days before you get test credentials.
Publishing an app to the Gong Collective is for partners only; new apps start in Private mode and can only be used within your own Gong account until published.
After submitting the Technology Partner Integration Review & Enablement form, Gong's team contacts you within five business days to help finalize the release and Collective listing.
OAuth setup must be done by a tech admin, who signs in with their own tech admin credentials during authorization; Gong doesn't support user-level OAuth and authenticates once at the company level.
findings.excerpt: Authentication happens once on a global level.

findings.statement: An OAuth app needs a redirect URI, a privacy policy link, a terms and conditions link, a help article link, and an authorization start page link.
Before publishing, you must provide trusted IP addresses that can access the integration - the app can't be published to the Gong Collective without these details.
You select the scopes your app needs; most use shared, company-wide access, though personal access is supported for a few AI/MCP-specific scopes.
The authorization context chosen when setting up OAuth can't be changed after setup.
By default, a company gets 3 API calls per second and 10,000 API calls per day; these limits can be raised by contacting Gong support.
After publication, changing scopes on a published OAuth app or troubleshooting an integration goes through a Gong support ticket rather than a self-serve settings change.
A Gong Technical Admin must approve the initial OAuth connection before Composio can manage or share it; Composio does not bypass Gong's admin requirement.
findings.sourceTitle: How Gong OAuth Works: Why It Requires a Technical Admin and How to Share Access

findings.statement: You create an integration under Admin center > Settings > Ecosystem > API, picking scopes and providing a name, descriptions, and logos; customers installing the app are asked to grant access to the entities covered by those scopes.
findings.excerpt: grant access to the entities accessed by these scopes

findings.statement: As an alternative to OAuth, a tech admin can generate an Access Key and Access Key Secret for direct Basic-auth API access instead.

claim.text: Getting a developer instance requires a partner application, and publishing an app so other Gong customers can use it is restricted to partners.
Publishing to the Gong Collective requires submitting a Technology Partner Integration Review & Enablement form and waiting on Gong's team.
OAuth setup is performed once, company-wide, only by a tech admin - there is no per-user authorization at all.

tierReason.text: Even getting a developer instance requires a partner application, and only partners can publish an app for other Gong customers to use.

claim.text: Gong's team follows up on a publish request within five business days of the Technology Partner Integration Review & Enablement submission.
It's unclear whether Composio offers Gong as a fully managed toolkit; either way, a Gong tech admin must still approve the initial OAuth connection.

whatYouLose.text: On a managed app, the consent screen shows the platform's name and brand instead of yours, and scopes and rate limits are typically fixed rather than something you control.

whenToSwitch.text: Switch to your own Gong OAuth app once you need your own branding, specific scopes, or your own rate limits.

flow.text: A Gong tech admin creates an integration, selects scopes, and completes a one-time, company-wide OAuth authorization; there is no per-user consent step.

appTypes.text: New apps default to Private (usable only in your own Gong account); making one available to other Gong customers requires publishing to the Gong Collective as a partner.

tokenNotes.text: Most scopes use shared, company-wide access rather than per-user tokens; only a few AI/MCP-specific scopes support personal access.

scopes.allows: Read and/or write access through Gong's MCP server.
scopes.neededFor: AI agent integrations built on Gong's MCP server.

claim.text: MCP integrations select the mcp:read and/or mcp:write scopes.

scopes.allows: Access data across the whole Gong account rather than one user's data.
scopes.neededFor: Most Gong integrations, since authorization is company-wide, not per user.

claim.text: Most scopes grant shared, company-wide access, and reaching external customers with any scope requires partner-gated publishing.
